clue.text: Money for basic food

definitions.meaning: slang for cash, as in dough
the staple loaf, the staff of life

explanation.surface: Cash spent on the bare essentials of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money and also the staple baked loaf eaten daily.

clue.text: The shaven man is shameless

definitions.meaning: with the face left bare of beard
brazen, without embarrassment

explanation.surface: A clean-shaven fellow is accused of brazenness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the word means having a bare face, which a shaven man has; its usual sense is brazen.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven man literally has a bare face; figuratively the word means brazen and unashamed.

clue.text: Achievement to turn to one's advantage

definitions.meaning: a daring deed or feat
to make use of something selfishly

explanation.surface: A feat that someone then milks for personal gain.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a bold feat; as a verb it means to use something for selfish profit.

clue.text: Sent back a little information

indicators.note: sent back tells us the phrase for a small amount is read from right to left

parts.note: a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A small snippet of news is returned to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns A TAD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, the raw material of information.

clue.text: Model actor in performance added embellishments

indicators.note: in places the reshaped letters inside the word for a performance

parts.note: a deed is an act performed

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so the letters of actor are reshaped

explanation.surface: A model actor dressed up the show with extra flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like an adjective praising the actor, but it is the anagram signal; 'in' then sets the reshaped letters (CORAT) within the deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have decorated something is to have adorned it with ornaments.

clue.text: Pulled up-with the shopping list

definitions.meaning: reprimanded or brought to heel
jokingly, summoned by being told what to order

explanation.surface: A meeting chair raps the gavel while holding a list of groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats the phrase as 'having had the order read out', as a shopping list would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Being called to order means being told to behave at a meeting, and a shopping list is an order to be called out.

clue.text: In times of peril extinguish your anger

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words peril extinguish

explanation.surface: When danger threatens, keep your temper under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to annoy or irritate them, so the verb sense matches anger.

clue.text: Parties disrupted by tramp

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters of parties are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Gatherings were broken up by a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' reads as a noun, a vagrant, but it is the verb for walking wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, to trudge along.

clue.text: Expedient for Venetian VIP to hold many captive

indicators.note: to hold means the Venetian leader's title grips the roman numeral inside it

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
D is 500 in Roman numerals, standing for a large number

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler keeps a crowd of prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a clever trick or stratagem, a convenient means to an end.

clue.text: Reckoned to have been set in thatch

indicators.note: in places the word for set inside the roofing material

parts.note: reed is a traditional thatching material
to put is to set or place

explanation.surface: Something was supposedly fixed into a thatched roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means thought or generally believed to be so.

clue.text: Extending oneself in the slammer

definitions.meaning: literally stretching out the body
serving a prison term; slammer is slang for jail

explanation.surface: A prisoner exercises in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: A stretch is slang for a prison sentence, so the phrase also means serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it is lengthening one's limbs; in slang a stretch is a jail sentence being served.

clue.text: Old heretic everyone backed in the name of Christ

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word for everyone inside the title for Christ

parts.note: Christ is called the Lord

indicators.note: backed means the word for everyone is turned round

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: An early dissenter whom all supported in Christ's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord is a standard title for Christ; 'backed' turns ALL round to LLA, and 'in' sets that within the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe in medieval England, condemned as heretics by the Church.

clue.text: Fail to sleep

definitions.meaning: to be a failure, as a show might
to drop down heavily and doze off

explanation.surface: Being unable to nod off.
explanation.definitionFit: A show that flops fails; to flop down is to collapse exhausted into rest.

clue.text: Skin complaint familiar to apiarists

definitions.meaning: urticaria, an itchy rash
beekeepers know their bee homes well

explanation.surface: Beekeepers often suffer from a particular rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives is the common name for nettle rash; beekeepers keep their colonies in boxes of that name.

clue.text: A psalm before the start of Evensong in church

parts.note: Ps is the standard abbreviation for psalm

indicators.note: the start of picks just the first letter of Evensong

explanation.surface: A psalm is sung just before the evening service in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a part found in a church, the vaulted recess at the east end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Utterly uninhibited Irish playwright

definitions.meaning: a pun on wild, completely unrestrained
Oscar, author of The Importance of Being Earnest

explanation.surface: A dramatist from Dublin with no restraint at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: the playwright's name is wild with an extra letter, a byword for unrestraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Dublin-born dramatist, and his name puns on wild, meaning unrestrained.

clue.text: Large cooking pot from the Southern States

definitions.meaning: a military camp kettle
nickname for the American South

explanation.surface: A big stewpot brought from the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: A dixie is British army slang for a large cooking pot or kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dixie is a soldier's big cooking pan, and Dixie names the former Confederate southern US.

clue.text: Only just in time with the mincer

definitions.meaning: leaving almost no margin
a mincer chops food very small

explanation.surface: A cook finishes the mincing just as guests arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leaving very little spare time; literally a mincer chops food finely.

clue.text: Embezzler put on trial and challenged

parts.note: a con, short for con man, is a swindler
tested means tried out

explanation.surface: A fraudster was tried in court and disputed the charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on trial' suggests a courtroom but means tried out, as an exam tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Contested means disputed or argued against.

clue.text: Unwillingness to be in Diana's situation

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, so Di's
position means situation

explanation.surface: Reluctance to swap places with Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposition can mean disinclination or reluctance to do something.

clue.text: Stamp enabling one couple to come into a fortune

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to come into places the pair inside the word for a fortune

parts.note: a mint is a vast sum of money
pr is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A postage stamp lets one pair inherit great wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a mark pressed into something, as a stamp leaves.

clue.text: I'm going to make bequests despite hostility

parts.note: I'll is the contraction for I will
to will is to leave property in a will

explanation.surface: Someone plans to leave legacies even though there is bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is enmity or malice toward someone.

clue.text: Philip Pirrip gets small English flute

parts.note: the full name of Pip, hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
E is a short form of English

explanation.surface: Dickens's hero acquires a little English instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple wind instrument, a tube blown like a flute.

clue.text: Offered to provide accommodation

definitions.meaning: put forward, as a candidate or money
to lodge a guest

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a proposal is to offer it; to put up a visitor is to house them.

clue.text: Vulgar, cold and discourteous

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
rude means impolite

explanation.surface: Coarse, frosty and impolite behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude means coarse or offensive in manner.

clue.text: A shade risque

definitions.meaning: a colour, like navy
slightly indecent, smutty

explanation.surface: A bit naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is a colour, and blue jokes or films are indecent.

clue.text: To speak indistinctly is a disgrace

definitions.meaning: to run words together
an insult or stain on reputation

explanation.surface: Mumbling is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: To slur is to mumble one's words; a slur is a slight on someone's character.

clue.text: Perch for a singer

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish, like the answer
a man with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: A place for a vocalist to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' suggests a seat but is a fish; the answer is another fish and also a deep-voiced singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a spiny fish related to the perch, and a singer with the lowest male voice.

clue.text: T-t-t term for a set of three

definitions.meaning: three letter Ts in a row, read as a tripled T
a trio or group of three

explanation.surface: A stammerer stumbles over the word for a trio.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered T-t-t shows the letter T three times, a 'triple T', which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is a group of three, such as three notes or three babies.

clue.text: The pragmatist is alert to change

indicators.note: to change means the letters of is alert are rearranged

explanation.surface: A practical person stays watchful for shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they are, like a practical, unsentimental person.

clue.text: Safe to get artificial material

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
sham means fake

explanation.surface: A locked box is opened to reveal fake fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is underworld slang for a safe, as in safecracker 'peterman'. Petersham is a thick ribbed ribbon or cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a heavy corded ribbon or cloth used for hatbands and waistbands.

clue.text: Unhappy about a large vegetable dish

indicators.note: about means the word for unhappy goes around the other letters

parts.note: sad means unhappy
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy about a big plate of greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad is a dish of raw mixed leaves and vegetables.
